The game is played over a variable number of rounds until a number of game-end achievements are collectively claimed by the players. The winner is the faction with the most Victory Points, which are obtained by researching technologies, improving their economy, controlling and colonizing systems, and through various achievements and events throughout the game. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 37 mn Complexity: 3 / 5 Play Beyond the Sun and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Icons 2 Technologies 3 Income Phase 4 Triggering the End of the Game, End Game Scoring, and Victory Points 5 Changes in BGA adaptation Icons [SHIP]/[SUPPLY]/[POPULATION]: Player cubes. Your [SUPPLY] are stored on your player board until converted to [SHIP] or [POPULATION]. [SUPPLY][ARROW][POPULATION]: Convert a Supply cube from the leftmost column into a Population cube. [ORE]: Ore. You can see how much Ore you have in the player pane. [LOSE_POPULATION]: Lose population (as part of the cost to perform an action). [I]/[II]/[III]/[IIII]: Technology of level 1/2/3/4. [RESEARCH][TECHX]: Research a technology. Requires a [POPULATION]. [VP]: Victory points. [COLONIZE]: Colonize a System. You must control the System with ships with a combined power of at least the System's colonize cost. Technologies The 4 types of Technologies have different characteristics, summarized below. A hybrid Technology generally contains characteristics of both of its types. 🟦 Scientific (blue): Ore production automation, research actions, and Ore bonuses 🟩 Economic (green): Food production automation, Population collection, and Ore collection 🟥 Military (red): Shipbuilding, movements, and upgrades 🟨 Commercial (yellow): Colonization actions, ship movements, and flexible actions Income Phase In the income phase, you may choose one of the following three options. Population: From each Supply Column above an uncovered space on the Population track, take one Supply and convert it to a Population Ore: Gain a quantity of Ore equal to the sum of uncovered Ore quantities on the Ore track. Resource trade: You may make as many of the following trades as you wish. Spend 3 Ore to turn 1 of your cubes from your leftmost Supply Column into a Population. Pay 1 ore to take 1 Spaceship from anywhere and turn it into a Population cube. Return a Population to the rightmost Supply Column with an empty space to gain an ore. Triggering the End of the Game, End Game Scoring, and Victory Points When enough discs have been placed on Achievements, the next round will be the final round of the game: 2 or 3 players: 3 Achievements claimed 4 players: 4 Achievements claimed Points are scored for the following Technologies 1 VP / Level I Technologies 2 VP / Level II Technologies 3 VP / Level III Technologies “Private Technologies” (from card bonuses) 2 VP / Level II Technologies 3 VP / Level III Technologies Level IV Technologies # VP / Level IV Technologies (differs per card) Automation Track Add all VP showing up to level reached After level 7, each additional level adds 1 VP Colonized Systems # VP / All System Cards (check bottom of each System Card) Uncolonized Outpost Discs (on System card or Shipyard Systems) 1 VP / Each Non-controllable Locations (Sol and Deep Space) 1 VP / Faction(s) with the highest military power (tied players get the same VP) Event Cards # VP / Event Card (Can provide VP. Found in some Achievement cards, attached to certain locations, or faction based) Achievements # VP / Specified by achievement (Can not get same achievement 2x) Tiebreaker 1. Combined production level (Food and Ore) 2. (If still tied after 1) The highest remaining Population cubes 3. (If still tied after 2) The highest remaining Ore Changes in BGA adaptation Minor changes were necessary to allow the game to work

[Rating: 2/10] Game suffers from same problem as similar games with action blocking. Turn order determines the winner. Adding an extra coal for 3/4 is a worthless bonus, considering how easy it is to get coal.

[Rating: 2/10] Mechanically interesting yet thematically dull. Despite supposedly being a sci-fi 4x it might as well be about tractor repair for all that it matters, a few words on cards is the extent of the thin veneer that sets the scene. [Rating: 2/10] Found my first few plays slightly...boring? Felt like the game was playing me at times, as though I had very little agency and was effectively forced into specific decisions against my will. I suspect I need to play it more to get a better handle on it. I'm very intrigued by the development of the tech tree and how the available actions and techs change the pace and position of the game, but it needs more thorough exploration.

[Rating: 3/10] This is one of those games that has perhaps the most irritating flaw I can find in a boardgame. An extremely shallow game that only gives the illusion of strategy and meaningful decision making. On a superficial take, this game might strike as a tight game that offers tough decisions with a fairly simple rule overhead. The problem is that the depth is just an illusion. The game all comes down to total randomness. [Rating: 3/10] Fastish tech tree game which is well designed but replay is an issue. + Quickish 90-100 minutes + Game end is variable increasing tension + Player boards are clear and dice/worker/ships are neat - Balance? Are some of the Factions better than others?   - Research Cards can be hard to read across the table - Game feels same-same on repeat plays. In fact after 3 plays I feel like I've explored it.

[Rating: 3/10] The game seems to force you to take research actions or your defeat is pretty much assured. I play space games to explore and interact with unique new worlds, not build a tech tree. That's part of a game, it shouldn't BE the game.

[Rating: 3/10] Totally adequate worker placement euro. Didn't like high density text cards being introduced again and again. Aesthetically the game resembles a sterile PowerPoint infographic. Mechanically it's nothing special either. The new techs basically do the same thing but more efficiently (not very interesting).
